source_text: SN 64 is a modern FPGA-based successor in concept to the TriStar 64's SNES functionality. It recreates the console-side SNES environment required by real cartridges while using an original Nintendo 64 or ModRetro M64 as the host/controller platform.
target: FPGA SNES environment with N64/M64 host/controllers
acceptance_evidence: Architecture review plus recorded real-cartridge operation on each unmodified host; host controller data demonstrably drives console-side SNES logic.
current_evidence: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-sn64-engineering-plan.md; fpga/rtl/sn64_console_candidate.sv; fpga/tests/tb_console_boot.sv (candidate and testbench; this entry does not assert a passing run); fpga/tests/tb_system.sv (whole-system power-on in simulation: N64 mailbox, ordered cartridge power, Si5351 lock, region decision, SNES program from a modelled cartridge reading the N64 controller image; see docs/design/system-integration.md)
open_dependencies: Integrated hardware, FPGA and bootstrap; both hosts.

source_text: The top slot is required to behave electrically and temporally like a genuine SNES/Super Famicom cartridge interface. Original cartridges, Super EverDrive X5/X6 and FXPAK Pro are first-class targets.
target: Electrically/timing-faithful full SNES slot and first-class cartridges
acceptance_evidence: Capture address/data/control/clock/reset/audio behavior against approved SNES timing limits and complete §14 matrix for original carts, X5, X6 and FXPAK Pro.
current_evidence: hardware/sn64/validation/interface-check.json (30 static checks; connector reference consistency only)
open_dependencies: Qualified socket, complete bridge, timing limits and physical cartridge tests.

acceptance_evidence: Verify pin maps, continuity and behavior for A0–23, D0–7, RD/WR/ROMSEL/IRQ/RESET, SYSTEM CLK/PHI2, PA0–7/PRD/PWR/WRAMSEL/REFRESH/EXPAND, CIC, +5 V/grounds, outer contacts and L/R audio. Record shared/open-drain drive ownership.
current_evidence: hardware/sn64/validation/interface-check.json (30 static checks; connector reference consistency only); docs/design/snes-interface-notes.md; fpga/tests/tb_cart_bridge.sv (bus ownership), hardware/sn64/cart-interface.kicad_sch with verify_cart_interface.py (62/62 contacts accounted); CIC data pins must-fix open
open_dependencies: Complete routing, bidirectional reset/CIC handling, audio integration and timing fixtures.

source_text: The cartridge domain is 5 V. FPGA pins must not rely on undocumented 5 V tolerance. Proper direction-controlled translation/buffering is required, including power-off isolation and contention-safe bidirectional data handling.
target: 5 V cartridge translation, isolation and bus turnaround
acceptance_evidence: Datasheet audit and worst-case timing calculation for each exact translator; measure legal logic levels, disabled/power-off leakage and contention-free OE/DIR read-write transitions with all power orders.
current_evidence: docs/design/translation-reuse-review.md (reference review; no final cartridge translator); docs/design/power-architecture.md (candidate architecture; no measured power budget); fpga/tests/tb_cart_bridge.sv (released clock at every owner change, contention monitor, fault build rejected); SN74LVC4245A translator sheet
open_dependencies: Exact translator/order code, voltage limits, delays, dead time and isolation circuit.

source_text: Cartridge +5 V uses a protected high-side load switch with soft start, current limiting, reverse-current blocking, voltage/current sensing and a hardware default-OFF state until configuration and rail checks pass.
acceptance_evidence: Verify high-side switch soft-start, current limit, reverse blocking and calibrated voltage/current sense; inject faults/configuration failure and prove hardware keeps power OFF until configuration and rail checks pass.
current_evidence: docs/design/power-architecture.md (candidate architecture; no measured power budget); fpga/tests/tb_power_sequencer.sv (default-off 5 V, ordered bring-up, latched faults; digital half only); hardware/sn64/power.kicad_sch + tools/verify_power_sheet.py (23 static checks, 11/11 mutations detected; attached to the root at the round-3 integration, ERC 0 errors; schematic only, no hardware)
open_dependencies: Final switch/monitor circuit, characterized loads, tolerance analysis and enable truth table.

source_text: The FPGA reproduces the console-side CPU, PPU, APU, memory map, DMA/HDMA, timers, arbitration and cartridge timing. With a physical cartridge inserted, cartridge ROM and cartridge-specific hardware remain outside the FPGA.
target: Console-side SNES CPU/PPU/APU/memory/timing with physical cart hardware
acceptance_evidence: Trace CPU, PPU, APU, map, DMA/HDMA, timers, arbitration and timing; compare functional traces and real output against test expectations while ROM/enhancement hardware reside in the inserted cartridge.
current_evidence: fpga/reports/evaluation.md and evaluation.json (2026-09-29, --mode all): 1,336-clock diagnostic passes reset/native CPU, modeled external reads/writes, WRAM, B-bus write and two-byte A-to-B DMA; PHI2 activity only. NTSC and PAL mode-bit runs use the same 46.56 ns clock; no PAL clock/video/audio qualification. Candidate synthesis and trial internal route complete; no physical hardware tested. Additional 1,089-clock WRAM bus regression passes current direct/two-mirror and data-port reads, B-to-A DMA and reset/pause source-valid gating; no electrical OE or physical bus qualification.
open_dependencies: PPU/APU/HDMA/timers/arbitration and full cartridge clock timing verification; physical ROM/enhancement-chip, graphics/audio and complete-system tests.

source_text: A mature open SNES FPGA core can be adapted, but its ROM-loader path must be replaced by a physical cartridge bridge.
target: Replace loader path with physical cartridge bridge
acceptance_evidence: Show active ROM/cart access reaches external address/data/control pins without loader remapping or an uploaded-ROM substitute; test physical reads/writes and cartridge-owned hardware arbitration.
current_evidence: fpga/reports/evaluation.md and evaluation.json (2026-09-29): modeled external read/write and DMA checks pass; raw $00:0010 mirrored-WRAM address is preserved at the wrapper cartridge interface. Corrupt low-byte injection fails the expected readback assertion. These are core/testbench checks, not electrical slot or real-cartridge validation. Additional 1,089-clock WRAM bus regression passes current direct/two-mirror and data-port reads, B-to-A DMA and reset/pause source-valid gating; no electrical OE or physical bus qualification.; fpga/tests/tb_cart_bridge.sv and tb_system.sv: physical-bus bridge replaces the loader path in simulation
open_dependencies: Physical D-bus reads/ownership, partially driven/open-bus behavior, peripheral-bus completeness, clocks, reset/CIC, translator turnaround/latency and cartridge-owned hardware arbitration.

source_text: SNES WRAM and other cycle-critical memories require deterministic latency. BRAM is preferred where practical, with synchronous external RAM only where timing is characterized.
acceptance_evidence: Document allocation and worst-case latency per memory; prefer BRAM with justification; simulate arbitration and close timing for any synchronous external RAM under simultaneous CPU/PPU/APU/DMA traffic.
current_evidence: fpga/reports/evaluation.md and evaluation.json (2026-09-29): WRAM readback, mirror-address regression and two-byte cartridge-to-WRAM DMA pass. Synthesis uses 139/208 EBRs (64 WRAM, 16+16 VRAM, 32 ARAM, 11 other); trial internal route reaches 29.91 MHz against 21.477273 MHz with unconstrained I/O. This is partial core evidence, not complete memory timing qualification. Additional 1,089-clock WRAM bus regression passes current direct/two-mirror and data-port reads, B-to-A DMA and reset/pause source-valid gating; no electrical OE or physical bus qualification.
open_dependencies: Worst-case simultaneous CPU/PPU/APU/DMA/HDMA memory latency and ARAM timing; full-product capacity/margins, final device/pins, external-memory decision and any external timing closure.

source_text: A low-jitter oscillator and FPGA clock management generate SNES timing. NTSC is the first validation target; PAL remains an architectural target. Cartridge clock outputs include tunable series termination footprints.
target: Low-jitter clocks, NTSC first, retained PAL and tunable outputs
acceptance_evidence: Oscillator/PLL plan supports NTSC and PAL; measure frequency, jitter, duty cycle and waveform limits under load; inspect populated/tunable series footprints at cartridge clock drivers.
current_evidence: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-sn64-engineering-plan.md; docs/design/clock-plan.md; fpga/tests/tb_clock_init.sv (Si5351 NTSC/PAL masters programmed and locked; region fixed at power-on)
open_dependencies: Exact clock source, quantified limits and both timing-mode evidence.

source_text: The lower edge presents SN 64 as an N64 cartridge. FPGA logic implements the timing-sensitive cartridge endpoint plus a mailbox/register protocol for a small N64-side bootstrap.
